text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Panic and bad weather brought chaos all over Cyprus. Hailstorms afflict Limassol and Paphos.
- The Democratic Rally and the Democratic Party have marathon consultations for cooperation of the two parties in December's parliamentary elections.
- Britain's envoy on Cyprus David Hannay will be bringing ideas with him on the Cyprus problem, not a plan.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Ambulance emergency. Forty people die a year because of poor response times.
- Stormy weather causes chaos in the Limassol and Paphos districts.
- Picking up the pieces. Over 300 aftershocks were recorded in the 24 hours after Wednesday's quake.
- The government predicts low growth and higher inflation for 1996.
HARAVGHI
- Britain's envoy David Hannay will arrive in Cyprus for talks on all aspects of the Cyprus problem.
- Justice minister says former working hours of the police force were squandering public funds.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Storms wreak havoc in Paphos and Limassol after earthquake.
- Experts are coming from Greece to assess damages and data from Wednesday's quake.
- Police discover 60 kilos of stolen dynamite.
SIMERINI
- Shock claim : Cancer patient who had just had surgery was left helpless at Limassol general hospital by staff during earthquake, to die minutes later of a heart attack.
- Panic-stricken parents rushed to pick up their children from school amid unsubstantiated rumours of a second, stronger earthquake.
- Hail the size of a walnut fell in Limassol and Paphos yesterday.
